source_text.ISS-0936: Issue ISS-0936 (local record docs/issues/ISS-0936.yaml, queue_ref Q-919, queue task 919, GH#2070; record may not yet be on this branch - PR #2071): scripts/uat_preflight.sh's qa-uat-env credential protocol (fetch_credential, ~line 290) expects the credential source's `token <user>` to print a line `Token: <jwt>`, but ai-dala-infra's qa-uat-env.sh `token <user>` prints a BARE JWT, so every actor login reports NO_PASSWORD. Fix: make fetch_credential accept a bare JWT line (three dot-separated base64url segments) as well as the `Token:` form. Add/adjust tests per project's existing preflight tests (none found under test/ -- TEST-DESIGNER decides a minimal in-repo test shape). Also update the script's header docs (qa-uat-env protocol paragraph) and scripts/README.md if they state the Token: form.

result.summary:
PASS. N1-N3 closed, verified by reading scripts/uat_preflight.sh. N1: every test command passes --idp-url equal to --base-url; script line 132 derives idp only when absent and realm GETs (lines 384-386) use idp, so runs are hermetic. T7 route list matches the script: /health x2 (line 378 and SHA probe lines 399-402), exactly two realm well-known paths (swiftroute from company_id, bpm-default), /api/v1/me/modules (line 333), /api/v1/tasks/inbox (non-candidate label, lines 555-558); /api/v1/tenants and /api/v1/version are skipped because admin_user needs 'admin-user' in cred_listing, which for qa-uat-env is scenario actor ids only (lines 284-289, 389-393); no process_id so no definitions GET. N2: T5 row is one well-formed table line using printf '%s
'; T5 note correctly says text=True (line 264) normalises CRLF so T5 is end-to-end, not an R1 exercise. N3: WSL-stub detection pinned as shared run_preflight/2 helper asserting header 'UAT PREFLIGHT  environment=qa' (script line 624, two spaces) with failure message naming launcher, first 500 chars and UAT_PF_BASH hint. Earlier gaps (flags lines 112-114, substrings lines 532/636, fixture, JWT length 49, Q2) not regressed. No implementation code beyond one signature and one regex; no TBD/deferral language.
